title: VPN lab: WireGuard and OpenVPN between two machines
summary: A server and a client on an isolated segment (172.20.1.0/24) with WireGuard and OpenVPN installed and nothing configured. The exercises build a WireGuard tunnel (10.10.0.0/24) and an OpenVPN static-key tunnel (10.20.0.0/24) by hand, watch the ciphertext on the segment and the plaintext inside the tunnel with tcpdump, and fence the server with iptables. Ported from qlab's vpn-lab.

exercises.title: WireGuard: keys, wg0.conf on both ends, the tunnel
exercises.text: Each end generates a key pair and only the public halves travel. The server listens on 51820/udp on the segment; the client names it as Endpoint. 10.10.0.1 is the server inside the tunnel, 10.10.0.2 the client.

commands: wg genkey | tee privatekey | wg pubkey > publickey && cat publickey    # the server's public key, for the client's [Peer]

sudo tee /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf >/dev/null <<EOF
[Interface]
Address = 10.10.0.1/24
ListenPort = 51820
PrivateKey = $(cat privatekey)

[Peer]
PublicKey = <CLIENT_PUBLIC_KEY>
AllowedIPs = 10.10.0.2/32
EOF
sudo wg-quick up wg0
wg genkey | tee privatekey | wg pubkey > publickey && cat publickey    # the client's public key, for the server's [Peer]

sudo tee /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf >/dev/null <<EOF
[Interface]
Address = 10.10.0.2/24
PrivateKey = $(cat privatekey)

[Peer]
PublicKey = <SERVER_PUBLIC_KEY>
Endpoint = 172.20.1.1:51820
AllowedIPs = 10.10.0.1/32
PersistentKeepalive = 25
EOF
sudo wg-quick up wg0
sudo wg show                        # latest handshake: a few seconds ago
ping -c3 10.10.0.1                  # the server, through the tunnel
sudo wg-quick down wg0 && ping -c1 -W2 10.10.0.1; sudo wg-quick up wg0    # no tunnel, no answer; back up in a second

exercises.title: OpenVPN with a static key
exercises.text: The simplest OpenVPN: one shared secret, a point-to-point tun. The server runs in the foreground so its log is visible; the client connects to the server's segment address on 1194/udp. Both ends name the cipher: OpenVPN 2.6 on OpenSSL 3 no longer has the static-key default BF-CBC ('Cipher BF-CBC not supported').

commands: sudo openvpn --genkey secret /etc/openvpn/static.key && sudo cat /etc/openvpn/static.key    # copy it to the client as /etc/openvpn/static.key

sudo tee /etc/openvpn/server.conf >/dev/null <<EOF
dev tun
ifconfig 10.20.0.1 10.20.0.2
secret /etc/openvpn/static.key
cipher AES-256-CBC
auth SHA256
port 1194
proto udp
keepalive 10 60
persist-tun
persist-key
verb 3
EOF
sudo openvpn --config /etc/openvpn/server.conf    # 'Initialization Sequence Completed' once the client is in

sudo tee /etc/openvpn/client.ovpn >/dev/null <<EOF
dev tun
remote 172.20.1.1 1194 udp
ifconfig 10.20.0.2 10.20.0.1
secret /etc/openvpn/static.key
cipher AES-256-CBC
auth SHA256
persist-tun
persist-key
verb 3
EOF
sudo openvpn --config /etc/openvpn/client.ovpn --daemon
ip -br addr show tun0

exercises.title: What the wire sees
exercises.text: With a tunnel up, tcpdump on the server shows UDP ciphertext on the segment NIC and plaintext ICMP inside wg0 or tun0: the point of a VPN in two captures.

commands: sudo timeout 10 tcpdump -ni vpn-lan udp port 51820    # WireGuard frames, while the client pings 10.10.0.1
sudo timeout 10 tcpdump -ni wg0                       # the same pings, in clear
sudo timeout 10 tcpdump -ni vpn-lan udp port 1194     # OpenVPN, while the client pings 10.20.0.1

exercises.title: Only the VPN and SSH get in
exercises.text: iptables on the server: established traffic, SSH (never lock the lab out: vmctl's own SSH comes through the NAT NIC), the two VPN ports, then DROP. Flushing the rules puts everything back.

commands: sudo iptables -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -p udp --dport 51820 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -p udp --dport 1194 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A INPUT -j DROP
sudo iptables -L INPUT -n -v
sudo iptables -F    # back to an open server
ping -c1 -W2 172.20.1.1 || echo 'dropped by the server, as intended'    # while the rules are in
ping -c1 -W2 10.10.0.1    # the tunnel still works: 51820/udp is allowed
